record.summary: An accessibility retrofit of the existing, below-grade 22nd Street Caltrain station -- the only regular-service Caltrain station without wheelchair access. The project adds ramps to both platforms plus wayfinding and safety improvements. Design is under way: SFCTA approved $1.3 million for the design phase in April 2026, Caltrain expects to complete design by summer 2027, and it is seeking construction funding to implement the project by June 2029. Sponsored by the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain) with SFCTA (Prop L) and FTA funding.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- a coarse placeholder box over the existing station's real location, not a traced footprint of the platforms or the planned ramps themselves (one ~305ft ramp on the northbound platform, one ~465ft ramp on the southbound platform, per the project's own design description).
notes.digitized_from: No Assessor block/lot exists for the existing 22nd St Caltrain station or its below-grade platforms (active rail right-of-way, the same reasoning already documented for the nearby 4th & King Station in the Mission Bay railyards record -- confirmed here too: DataSF's 'Parcels - Active and Retired' Socrata dataset has no parcel at this location). No Caltrain/Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board GIS shapefile or site-plan figure was available, so this is a coarse locational box near the real DataSF street-centerline address range for 22nd St at Pennsylvania Ave/Indiana St (DataSF's official street centerlines), where the existing below-grade station sits.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Active Caltrain rail right-of-way; not on the Assessor's secured roll, the same situation as the existing 4th & King Street Station (mapped in Pier & Point's Mission Bay railyards record).
notes.regulatory_context: The Caltrain 22nd Street Station is the railroad's only regular-service station that is not wheelchair accessible: its platforms sit about 25 ft below street level, reachable only by stairs. Sponsor: Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain); funded in part through SFCTA's Prop L. Total project cost per SFCTA's April 2026 Board Packet: $19,134,000 (Planning/Conceptual Engineering $734,000 already spent via Prop K; Design Engineering $1,300,000 via Prop L, allocated 2026-04-28; Construction $17,100,000, an engineer's estimate at 30% design). The FTA's 'All Stations Accessibility Program' separately awarded the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board $14.1 million for this project's ADA improvements, announced 2026-09-10 -- matching almost exactly the funding gap SFCTA's own April 2026 plan had left as 'Planned TBD'.

facts.value: Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain), with funding from SFCTA (Prop L) and the FTA

One ramp on the northbound platform (about 305 ft long, 6.5% slope) and one on the southbound platform (about 465 ft long, 6.1% slope), plus tactile strips, lighting and signage. Platforms sit about 25 ft below street grade, currently reachable only by stairs.

open_questions: This record's placement under Pier 70 rather than Potrero Power Station reflects a roughly equal real-world distance (about 400-450m to each tracked boundary) plus the station's more established association with the Dogpatch/Pier 70 corridor in transit planning -- not a precise geometry test against a real station footprint (no Assessor parcel or site-plan figure exists to test against; the map shape is a coarse placeholder box; see its accuracy note).
No construction start date is confirmed beyond the spring 2028 target implied by SFCTA's own milestone table; this could shift given design is only at an early stage as of 2026-09-28.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the summary and the completion milestone no longer give a spring 2028 construction start, a mid/late 2029 completion or the $19,134,000 total, because the April 14, 2026 SFCTA board packet they came from refuses automated fetches and could not be re-read; they now follow SFCTA's readable April 28, 2026 post (design by summer 2027, construction funding sought to implement the project by June 2029). The $19,134,000 cost entry and its breakdown stay, marked as not re-checked; the owner can open the packet in a browser to confirm them.
